member.name: FolderConfig
member.para: Why the folders' settings are layered by re-parsing rather than merged. A merge would need to know, for every option, whether a second value replaces the first or adds to it - --model replaces, --custom adds, --chapter-phrase adds - which is knowledge the parser already has and nothing else should have a second copy of. Putting the folders' tokens in front of the command line and parsing the whole thing gives the right answer for every option by construction, including options added later, and cost nothing to build: it is the same mechanism uses for an explicit --config. The price is a parse per file that has a folder file, which is microseconds against a book.

Why run-wide settings are refused rather than applied (the user's call, 2026-08-20, from two alternatives that were on the table). The tool loads its Whisper model once for the whole run, before the first file, and holds one log, one progress renderer, one mode and one file selection. Honouring --model from a folder would mean reloading gigabytes at a folder boundary and growing a per-file component into the resume fingerprint; honouring --recurse or --filter from a folder is incoherent, since those decided which files exist before any folder was read. The alternative considered and rejected was to apply run-wide options from whichever folder was reached first, which is defensible in code and impossible to explain in a manual.

What that boundary costs, stated plainly: --max-chapters is refused even though it is a per-file judgement, because it is read where a file is skipped rather than where it is detected, and this feature deliberately reaches only the detection. If a folder ever genuinely needs it, that is a decision to extend the per-file options into 's own skip logic, not to move the line quietly.
